project_title: Custom Beverage Mixing Device Prototype (DJ-Style Matcha Mixer)

project_metadata.job_title: Custom Beverage Mixing Device Prototype (DJ-Style Matcha Mixer)
project_metadata.job_description:
We are looking for a mechanical/product engineer to help design and prototype a custom beverage mixing device for live event use.

This device is a dual-station matcha mixing system inspired by DJ turntables, designed to create a visually engaging experience while mixing powdered beverages (matcha).

Project Overview:

The device will include:

Two circular mixing stations (“decks”)
Motorized whisking mechanism in each station
Independent speed control for each side
Central control panel (knobs/switches)

The goal is to create a functional prototype that:

Mixes matcha smoothly (similar to handheld electric whiskers)
Looks visually impressive for live events
Is safe and practical for repeated use

Key Requirements:

1. Dual Mixing System

Two independent mixing bowls (8–12 inches diameter)
Food-safe materials (stainless steel preferred)

2. Mixing Mechanism

Motor-driven whisk or similar solution
Must create smooth, frothy consistency
Variable speed control

3. Control Interface

Speed control knobs (one per mixing station)
Power switch
Simple, intuitive layout

4. Build Considerations

Use off-the-shelf components where possible (for prototype)
Durable and stable structure
Easy to clean

5. Noise Level

Should not be excessively loud (used in event environments)

Design Direction:

We will provide a visual concept (DJ-style layout), but we are not locked into exact design details.

We are looking for someone who can:

Translate concept into a working prototype

Suggest the simplest and most cost-effective approach

Deliverables:

Concept refinement / recommendations
Basic CAD or design drawings
Parts list (BOM)
Prototype guidance (or build if capable)

Ideal Candidate:

Experience with consumer product prototyping
Mechanical + basic electrical knowledge
Experience with motors / mixing devices is a plus
Practical, solution-oriented mindset

Timeline:

We are aiming for a working prototype within 4–6 weeks

Budget:

$2,000–$8,000 for initial prototype phase, flexible depending on approach.

When Applying:

Please include:

Similar projects (if any)
Your approach to building this
Estimated timeline

The image attached represents the visual concept and layout we are aiming for (DJ-style dual mixing station).

We are not locked into this exact design — we are looking for your expertise to engineer a functional prototype that achieves this look and experience.

Priority is:

Smooth, high-quality matcha mixing (similar to handheld electric whisk)
Dual mixing stations (like DJ decks)
Visually engaging for live events

We are open to using existing components for the first prototype to reduce cost and timeline.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The system uses a 120v to 12v 20A Dc power supply with separate PWM speed controllers. Each mixing station has a 12v 200rpm motor linked through a 3/8" shaft coupling to a 3/8" stainless steel shaft. That shaft drives the wire wisk for mixing and frothing the matcha. The electronics receive cooling from 120mm fans. On the plumbing side, every 2.5 quart stainless steel bow has a 5/16 barb outlet. A #2 silicone stopper provides a leak-proof press-fit connection. The 5/16 silicone tubing travels from the barb union inside the stopper to the 3/4" ght adapter, which screws directly onto the push-style beverage spigots.

messages.text: The revised build plan remains similar to the original, with some changes to accommodate the new spout and solenoid valve. A stainless steel bulkhead threads into the opening at the bottom of the bowl. A stainless steel nipple then attaches to it, forming a quick-release system so the bowls can be swapped easily. That nipple slides into a silicone plug to form a watertight seal, while the opposite side of the plug accepts the 1/2 inch 90 degree connector. The connector will lead to a solenoid valve that sends the matcha to the stainless steel spout when a button is pressed.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001] — I reviewed the BOM, and I really like the overall direction. It matches exactly what I was hoping for.

Before we proceed, I’d like your thoughts on a few items:

• Motors — I’m concerned that 200 RPM may be slightly too low to produce a strong, frothy matcha texture. Would increasing the RPM make sense while still preserving enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality, would a stainless steel or milk-frother-style head work better than the resin whisk?

• Spout — I want to continue with the solenoid solution. For both texture and the visual experience, the pour needs to be clean, controlled, and seamless through the full sequence (mix → open → pour).

• Splash / mess control — this is especially important for events. I want to ensure:
– little to no splashing while mixing
– a smooth, controlled stream from the spout without sputtering
– no drips after the valve closes
– effective seals that prevent anything from leaking into the base
– a splash guard or lip around the bowl if one is necessary

• Cleaning — if possible, the bowls and spout parts should either be removable or easy to clean.

I’m very happy with everything else. I’d like to hear what you think about these points and whether you would change anything before we finalize the BOM.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
On the motors, I believe your concern about speed is correct. I've chosen new motors rated for 1000RPM. The PWM controller will continue to provide adjustment from 0 through 1000 while retaining enough torque to mix the liquids.

The whisk is the difficult part because there aren't many choices that satisfy our requirements. We need a reasonably large mixing head so the entire bowl mixes properly. The bowl is approximately 9 inch in diameter, but the plastic mixing head included on the BOM measures only about 2.4" in diameter. By comparison, my original wire-whisk suggestion was approximately 4.5" in diameter. Although it is advertised for a 6qt bowl, I believe it could still perform well in our smaller bowl. A head resembling those used on handheld electric frothers/mixers would probably be ideal, but those are available only in very small sizes.

I don't expect splashing to present a problem. If the action becomes too aggressive, the motor speed can be adjusted while it is operating. As you proposed, we can also add a basic splash guard if splashing does occur.

For cleaning, the current design allows the bowl to be removed very easily. The custom spout will also be designed for removal so it can be cleaned without difficulty.

Overall, we are almost ready, and I'll update the motor to 1000rpm. For the whisk, perhaps we should select 2 different styles and test them to determine which performs best. The whisk should be among the simplest parts to replace with a new design if necessary, and a basic adapter should enable nearly any whisk to connect to our system.

With the increased RPM, I do want to ensure that:
• splashing remains controlled
• mixing stays smooth rather than becoming excessively aggressive at higher settings

If necessary, I’m open to installing a splash guard or fine-tuning the whisk position / bowl depth so the machine operates cleanly.

Before moving ahead with the parts order, I want to verify a few last details:

• Motor performance — I like having the flexibility of 3000 RPM, but I want to ensure we can tune the speed for smooth mixing without creating excessive splashing at the higher settings.

• Solenoid flow — because the valves are on/off, do you anticipate a smooth pour when they open, or could the initial release be too sudden? The goal is a clean, controlled pour without splashing.

• Power supply — when both motors, the solenoids, and the fans are operating under load, will we remain comfortably inside the capacity of the 12V 20A power supply?

• Splash control — given the higher RPM, can you confirm that the whisk location, bowl depth, and overall configuration will keep the operation clean? For events, I want the machine to be as splash-proof and mess-free as possible.

Everything else looks great. I just want these points fully resolved before the order is submitted.

Let me know what you think.

Moving to a higher-output power supply would probably be prudent, as it would lower the risk of overheating or overloading. For the same overheating concern, using higher-rated PWM controllers would also be beneficial.

As for the spouts, I will fabricate them from 1/32 stainless steel. That material is listed at the very bottom of the BOM.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I fully understand why the uncertain timeline is frustrating and why you urgently need to manage your business schedule. I’m sorry that I was unavailable over the weekend. To provide an accurate delivery schedule today, I needed to carefully go back through the history of our design decisions.

To explain the build’s current status, the short video I provided on June 6th showed only an internal engineering test of the raw internal plumbing while it was disassembled. Its purpose was to confirm that the core mechanics function flawlessly, not to present the completed housing.

During our discussion about aesthetic upgrades on June 7th, I explained that adding embedded custom text, measurement rings, logos on both sides, and LED lighting would mean completely scrapping the physical chassis that I had already built according to your initially approved specifications. Making extensive visual modifications before testing the internal mechanics under load is very risky. We could finish an attractive shell and then discover that a mechanical component must be changed, which would require the physical base to be discarded again.

To remove the uncertainty and safeguard your investment, we have to select one of these two paths today:
